blueprints.primary_construct: Explain concrete ordered actions and close with a relevant summary or recommendation while preserving a clear opening
blueprints.prompt_text: Your university is holding a used-book exchange. Explain to a student volunteer how to run it: state the aim, describe two or three concrete steps with relevant details, and end with a brief summary or practical recommendation. Prepare silently for 60 seconds and speak for 45 to 60 seconds. Give your first answer without a model, hints, notes, or feedback.

criteria.description: Connects two or three concrete actions with relevant details
Closes with a concise summary or practical recommendation linked to the explanation

required_meaning_units: ordered concrete actions with relevant detail
semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any realistic process that addresses the assigned situation

blueprints.primary_construct: Track a speaker's concern and the purpose of the proposed response
blueprints.prompt_text: Listen to the dialogue without the transcript. Explain Nora's concern, Sam's proposed arrangement, and why he thinks it will help. You may listen twice and answer in Chinese or simple English.

material.transcript_text:
Nora: Our group presentation is next Tuesday, but I cannot attend a long rehearsal on Friday. I have a lab session until five, and I still need time to finish my slides.
Sam: Why not send us your slides on Thursday? We can check the order online. Then we could have a short rehearsal on Monday evening. That would let us test the transitions without keeping everyone busy for hours.

criteria.description: Identifies Friday lab conflict and need to finish slides
Links Thursday online slide review and short Monday rehearsal to testing transitions with less time commitment

required_meaning_units: Friday lab and unfinished slides limit availability
short Monday rehearsal tests transitions with less time
semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any Chinese or English wording preserving the concern-response-purpose relationship

blueprints.primary_construct: Identify an expository text's main line and explain how a detail supports it
blueprints.prompt_text: Read the passage. Summarize its problem, trial and result. Explain why the staff recommend limiting bookings, and why they cannot yet be certain that the system works during busy periods.

material.text: A university tested online bookings for its campus printers. Previously, students waited in a single queue and could not predict how long printing would take. During a three-week trial, students could reserve a ten-minute slot. Average waiting time fell, and most participants said planning was easier. However, several booked slots were left unused, while students without bookings still had to wait. Staff therefore proposed limiting each student to one active booking and cancelling a reservation if the student was more than five minutes late. The trial took place early in the term, when relatively few assignments were due. Staff said they needed another trial near submission deadlines before deciding whether to keep the system.

criteria.description: Identifies uncertain waiting, booked slots, reduced waits and proposed changes
Links unused slots to booking restrictions and light early-term demand to uncertainty near deadlines

required_meaning_units: bookings reduced waits and improved planning
unused bookings motivate limits and late cancellation
busy deadline periods were not tested
semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any wording preserving the causal and limiting relationships
